page: Vultr voc-c-32c-64gb-500s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server powered by an AMD EPYC processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores with 2 threads per core, operating at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz. The system is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 2.0 GB per core ratio, and includes 500 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage.

In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates strong computational capabilities. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance ranks in the top tier (top 10%), while the multi-core CPU performance is positioned in the top 25%. Cryptographic execution is also a strength, with the PassMark CPU encryption test scoring in the top 25%. For specialized workloads, the server achieves top-tier performance in text generation for small (135M) language models, alongside strong image processing capabilities. Memory bandwidth and database operations remain within the average range.

The 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio positions this instance as a compute-heavy resource, offering high compute density relative to memory capacity. While the dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent execution without resource contention, workloads requiring massive memory footprints may find the 64.0 GB memory limit restrictive. This hardware profile is suited for compute-bound tasks, image processing, cryptographic workloads, and small-scale language model inference.
